commands.name: project
commands.about: Manage registered projects

commands.name: list
commands.about: List all registered projects and their sources. Use this first to see what's indexed and searchable before calling search_code or search_knowledge.

commands.name: add
commands.about: Register a new project container. Add sources to it with source add.
commands.after:
Example:
  scrybe project add --id myrepo --desc "My project"

commands.name: update
commands.about: Update a project's description.
commands.after:
Example:
  scrybe project update myrepo --desc "Updated description"
options: Project identifier (flag, backward-compat alias for positional)

commands.name: remove
commands.about: Unregister a project and drop all its source tables (vector data deleted).
commands.after:
Examples:
  scrybe project remove myrepo
  scrybe project rm myrepo
options: Project identifier (flag, backward-compat alias for positional)

commands.name: source
commands.about: Manage indexable sources within a project

commands.name: list
commands.about: List all sources (optionally filter by project).
commands.after:
Examples:
  scrybe source list
  scrybe source list -P myrepo

commands.name: add
commands.about: Add an indexable source to a project (code repo, GitLab/GitHub issues, etc.) and auto-enqueue a reindex. Returns a job_id to poll with reindex_status.
commands.after:
Examples:
  scrybe source add -P myrepo -S code --type code --root /path/to/repo --languages ts,vue
  scrybe source add -P myrepo -S tickets --type ticket --provider gitlab --url https://gitlab.example.com --project 42 --token $TOKEN
  scrybe source add -P myrepo -S gh-issues --type ticket --provider github --project owner/repo --token '${SCRYBE_GITHUB_TOKEN}'
options: Absolute path to repo root (required for type=code)
Provider base URL (required for GitLab; optional for GitHub — defaults to https://api.github.com)
Provider-scoped project identifier: GitLab numeric id or path; GitHub owner/repo
[deprecated: use --project] GitLab project ID or path

commands.name: update
commands.about: Update an existing source's config — e.g. refresh a token, change root path, or update language hints. Only the fields you provide are changed.
commands.after:
Examples:
  scrybe source update -P myrepo -S tickets --token $NEW_TOKEN
  scrybe source update -P myrepo -S tickets --gitlab-token $NEW_TOKEN  # deprecated
options: New personal access token (literal or ${VAR} form)
[deprecated: use --token] New GitLab personal access token
[deprecated: use --project] GitLab project ID or path

commands.name: remove
commands.about: Remove a source from a project and drop its vector table.
commands.after:

commands.name: list

Example:

commands.name: index-ephemeral
commands.about: Index an open MR's remote branch under a throwaway '_ephemeral/' label, for searching a PR's content without disturbing the project's normally indexed branches. scrybe does NOT fetch — fetch the ref yourself first (e.g. 'git fetch origin <branch>'), then call this tool; it errors clearly if the ref isn't resolvable locally. Label rule: defaults to '_ephemeral/mr-<branch>' (override with 'label', still forced under the '_ephemeral/' prefix). If 'branch' is already a full ref (starts with 'refs/' or 'origin/'), it is used as the content source directly and the label is derived from its last path segment. Never creates a pinned_branches entry and is invisible to the fetch-poller and 'branch pin' — call drop_ephemeral to remove it once the MR closes.
commands.after:
Example:
  scrybe index-ephemeral -P myrepo --branch mr-42-feature
options: Already-fetched MR branch, or a full ref
Override the ephemeral label (still forced under _ephemeral/)

commands.name: drop-ephemeral
commands.about: Remove an '_ephemeral/' label created by index_ephemeral: deletes its branch_tags/branch_state/hashes (via deleteBranch) then runs a source-scoped gc to reclaim the now-orphaned chunks (chunks still shared with another indexed branch survive). Refuses to drop any label that isn't under the '_ephemeral/' prefix — this verb must never remove a real branch like 'dev' or 'master'. Idempotent: dropping an already-gone label is a no-op success.
commands.after:
Example:
  scrybe drop-ephemeral -P myrepo --label _ephemeral/mr-42

commands.name: search
commands.about: Search code or knowledge sources

commands.name: code
commands.about: Semantically search code in a project using natural language. Use list_projects first to confirm the project has an indexed code source.
commands.after:
Example:
  scrybe search code -P myrepo "auth flow"

commands.name: knowledge
commands.about: Semantically search GitLab issues, webpages, or other knowledge sources indexed in a project. Use list_projects first to confirm the project has indexed knowledge sources. Optionally filter by source_id (specific source) or item_types. Known item_types: "ticket" = GitLab issue bodies; "ticket_comment" = individual issue comments (each with its own author, timestamp, and #note_NNN deep-link). Omit item_types to search both. Use ["ticket_comment"] to find architectural decisions made in comments, or ["ticket"] to find/deduplicate issue bodies.
commands.after:
Example:
  scrybe search knowledge -P myrepo "login issue"

commands.name: branch
commands.about: Manage indexed branches and pinned branches

commands.name: list
commands.about: List branches that have been indexed for a project's sources. Each code source maintains separate indexed chunks per branch. Non-code sources (tickets) always use the branch sentinel '*'.
commands.after:
Examples:
  scrybe branch list -P myrepo
  scrybe branch list -P myrepo --pinned

commands.name: pin
commands.about: Add (or replace) pinned branches on a code source. mode='add' (default) merges with the existing list; mode='set' replaces it. Returns warnings if pinned count exceeds 20 or if a branch has no ignore coverage.
commands.after:
Example:
  scrybe branch pin -P myrepo feature/my-feature

commands.name: unpin
commands.about: Remove branches from the pinned list. Silently no-ops on branches not currently pinned. Does NOT delete indexed data — run scrybe gc to remove orphan chunks.
commands.after:
Examples:
  scrybe branch unpin -P myrepo feature/my-feature
  scrybe branch unpin -P myrepo --all --yes
args: Branch names to unpin (omit to use --all)

commands.name: index
commands.about: Index or reindex a project (all sources) or specific sources
commands.after:
Examples:
  scrybe index -P myrepo
  scrybe index -P myrepo -S primary,gitlab-issues
  scrybe index --all
  scrybe index -P myrepo -f -S primary
  scrybe index -P myrepo --detach  # submit and exit (CI use)
options: Full reindex (clears and rebuilds from scratch)
Branch name to index (default: current HEAD for code sources)
Git ref to read content from (e.g. 'origin/dev'). When set, content is read from this ref while --branch remains the stored label. Defaults to --branch.
Submit to daemon and return immediately (prints job_id, no progress stream)

commands.name: gc
commands.about: Remove orphan chunks not referenced by any indexed branch
commands.after:
Examples:
  scrybe gc --dry-run
  scrybe gc
options: Limit GC to a specific project (default: all projects)

commands.name: start
commands.about: Run the daemon attached to this terminal (use `daemon up` to background it)
commands.after:
Examples:

  scrybe daemon start   # run attached — Ctrl+C stops it (used by OS autostart hooks)

commands.after:
Example:

  scrybe daemon stop --force   # don't wait for an in-flight reindex
options: Abandon the drain: send a second SIGTERM so the daemon exits immediately, cancelling in-flight reindex jobs

commands.name: ignore
commands.about: Edit per-source private ignore rules (stored in DATA_DIR — never committed)
commands.after:
Opens an interactive wizard to select a project and source, then opens
your $EDITOR on the private ignore file. After saving, you can choose
to reindex the source immediately to apply the new rules.

The file uses gitignore syntax and lives in:
  <DATA_DIR>/ignores/<project_id>/<source_id>.gitignore

It is applied additively on top of .gitignore and .scrybeignore.

Examples:
  scrybe ignore                            # interactive wizard
  scrybe ignore edit                       # same (alias subcommand)
  scrybe ignore list                       # list all private ignore files (stdout)
  scrybe ignore get -P myrepo -S primary   # print one file's content (stdout)

commands.name: edit

commands.about: Print the private ignore file content for a source (stdout, non-interactive)
